What is another major bacillus species implicated in human disease?

cohort_answer.text: B. anthracis: (non)Motility, (non)hemolysis, Gamma phage testing or PCR, and pen S. Non motile, spore forming, non hemolysis. Other bacillus involved in human diseases: B. cereus: gastroenteritis, bacteremia. B. subtilis = rare cause of pneumonia, bacteremia, septicemia (usually in patients with hematologic malignancy or some other severe immune compromise) and may cause foodborne disease (diarrheal illness similar to B. cereus). B. licheniformis = associated with outbreak of bacteremia in immunocompromised due to contaminated cotton wool, and a well-established cause of central-line infections. All other species are motiles or +/- motil. R to pen except B. cereus biovar anthracis.
